Scene:
Same square frame, same plaza, same cathedral silhouette, same camera position and lens as the reference. Time is midnight under a clear sky; stars faintly visible in the gap above the building. Plaza is dry.

Subject:
The identical green-glass cathedral from the reference. All interior lighting has been changed to cool blue — as if a full choir of blue candles fills every chapel. The cathedral reads as a deep glacial lantern against the black sky. Outside, a single pool of warm tungsten streetlamp light in the lower left provides warm-cool contrast and rim-lights the nearest buttress.

Important details:
Preserve exact cathedral silhouette, plaza geometry, and pedestrian positions from the reference (pedestrians now read as silhouettes against the glowing building). Cool interior light color temperature ~6500K, reflected through green glass biases toward teal. Thin cold mist hugs the plaza floor, catching the base of the cathedral in a pale halo. No rain.

Use case:
Second image in the glass cathedral cycle. Demonstrates cold interior lighting through the same translucent building.

Constraints:
PRESERVE the reference image cathedral silhouette, camera angle, plaza, and pedestrian positions. No readable text, no watermark, no logos, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio, no lightning, no moon, no stylized illustration.
